reference_sql:
SELECT customer_id
FROM orders
WHERE channel = 'web'
  AND customer_id IS NOT NULL
  AND order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-05-12 00:00:00'
  AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-05-19 00:00:00'
INTERSECT
SELECT customer_id
FROM orders
WHERE channel = 'store'
  AND customer_id IS NOT NULL
  AND order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-05-12 00:00:00'
  AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-05-19 00:00:00'
alternatives: SELECT DISTINCT w.customer_id FROM orders w JOIN orders s ON s.customer_id = w.customer_id WHERE w.channel = 'web' AND s.channel = 'store' AND w.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-05-12 00:00:00' AND w.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-05-19 00:00:00' AND s.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-05-12 00:00:00' AND s.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-05-19 00:00:00'

WITH week_orders AS (SELECT customer_id, channel FROM orders WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL AND order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-05-12 00:00:00' AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-05-19 00:00:00') SELECT customer_id FROM week_orders WHERE channel = 'web' INTERSECT SELECT customer_id FROM week_orders WHERE channel = 'store'

other_way.sql: SELECT DISTINCT w.customer_id FROM orders w JOIN orders s ON s.customer_id = w.customer_id WHERE w.channel = 'web' AND s.channel = 'store' AND w.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-05-12 00:00:00' AND w.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-05-19 00:00:00' AND s.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-05-12 00:00:00' AND s.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-05-19 00:00:00'
other_way.tradeoff: A self-join on customer_id finds the same customers, but it pairs every web order with every store order before DISTINCT.
